questions.question: Write a note on fermentation during bread making ? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on fermentation during bread making.
  • Ans :
  • • Fermentation is the process where yeast acts on sugars in the dough.
  • • It is an anaerobic process that takes place without oxygen.
  • • It starts immediately after mixing and continues during inter proofing and
  • final proofing.
  • • The main purpose of fermentation is to produce carbon dioxide gas which
  • makes the dough rise.
  • • It also helps to develop flavour and aroma in the bread.
  • • Fermentation improves the dough texture and makes it soft.
  • • Ideal temperature for fermentation is between 24°C and 30°C.
  • • Ideal humidity is about 70% to 75%.
  • • These conditions are best for yeast activity and proper fermentation.
  • • Usually 2% baker’s yeast (based on flour weight) is used.
  • • Too little yeast causes slow fermentation.
  • • Too much yeast gives sour Flavors and poor texture.
  • • During fermentation, glucose (sugar) is converted by yeast into carbon
  • dioxide and alcohol.
  • • Carbon dioxide makes the dough rise, and alcohol evaporates during baking.
  • • Well-fermented dough becomes light, soft, and airy.
  • • Bread made from properly fermented dough has good volume, taste, and
  • texture.

questions.question: What is sugarcane ? Write down its nutritive value. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is sugarcane? Write down its nutritive value.
  • Sugarcane
  • Sugarcane is the chief source of sugar. It contains 12–15% sugar (mainly sucrose). In India,
  • about 80–90% of sugarcane is used for the manufacture of sugar, gur, khandsari, and
  • other products.
  • It is also used for making beverages, chewing cane, and various sugar products.
  • Nutritive Value of Sugarcane Juice
  • Nutrient Amount
  • Energy 40–60 kcal
  • Carbohydrates 10–15 g
  • Sugars (Sucrose, Glucose, Fructose) 9–13 g
  • Protein 0.1 g
  • Fat 0 g
  • Nutrient Amount
  • Fiber 0 g
  • Calcium 10–15 mg
  • Potassium 150–200 mg
  • Iron 0.3 mg
  • Magnesium 10–12 mg
  • • Sugarcane contains sucrose, glucose, and fructose.
  • • Used for white sugar, gur (jaggery), khandsari, and molasses.
  • • 5–10% of sugarcane is used for chewing.
  • • It provides quick energy due to high sugar content.
  • • Good source of potassium, calcium, and iron.

questions.question: How cocoa powder is produced ? / [CO3] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• How cocoa powder is produced?
  • Steps in Cocoa Powder Production
  • Harvesting
  • Ripe cocoa pods are cut from the trees using knives or machetes.
  • Pod Opening
  • The pods are split open and the beans with pulp are removed.
  • Fermentation
  • Beans are fermented for 5–7 days to develop flavour, reduce bitterness, and remove pulp.
  • Drying
  • Fermented beans are dried in the sun or dryers until moisture reaches 6–7%.
  • Breaking and Winnowing
  • Dried beans are cracked (breaking) and shells are removed to get cocoa nibs.
  • Alkalisation (Dutching)
  • Nibs are treated with alkali (e.g., potassium carbonate) to improve colour, flavour, and
  • dispersibility.
  • Roasting
  • Alkalised nibs are roasted at 120–150°C to enhance flavour and reduce moisture.
  • Nib Grinding
  • Roasted nibs are ground into a thick paste called cocoa liquor (or cocoa mass).
  • Liquor Treatment (Pressing)
  • Cocoa liquor is pressed to separate cocoa butter.
  • The solid cake left behind is used for cocoa powder.
  • Pulverisation
  • The cocoa cake is crushed and ground into fine cocoa powder.
  • Packing
  • The cocoa powder is sieved and packed in airtight, moisture-proof containers or bags
  • to prevent spoilage.
  • Storage
  • Packed powder is stored in cool, dry conditions, away from light and strong odours to
  • maintain quality.
  • Transport
  • Finished cocoa powder is transported in sealed containers or cartons to protect it from
  • moisture, heat, and contamination.

  • Soft candy is a type of confectionery that is chewy, moist, and flexible. It has a smooth
  • texture and does not break easily when bent. Examples include toffees, caramels, and jelly
  • candies. Soft candies are made by heating sugar and other ingredients to a specific
